\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Noise stability bounded by bivariate stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability_le_bivariate_integral}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability_le_bivariate_integral}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianBivariateStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_correlatedGaussianMeasure_mul, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianBivariateStability_comp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.mul_le_gaussianBivariateStability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\rho<1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be
measurable with $0\le f(x)\le1$ for every $x$. Its Gaussian noise stability is at most
the expectation of the bivariate Gaussian stability at the pair of values $(f(X),f(Y))$,
where $(X,Y)$ has the correlated Gaussian measure with coordinate correlation $\rho$.
\end{theorem}
